strings.name: Kent Beck
strings.summary: Kent Beck advanced Extreme Programming and test-driven development, co-created JUnit with Erich Gamma and is one of the Agile Manifesto’s 17 co-authors. His tools and books promote short feedback cycles, testing and code tidying. More recently he has discussed trust in AI-assisted development. These methods and projects grew through many practitioners and communities.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. First publication and copyright years are distinguished. Test-first thinking is not described as his sole original invention; collaborators retain credit.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced Extreme Programming, test-driven development and agile practices, broadly influencing how modern software teams work.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned bachelor’s and master’s degrees in computer and information science at the University of Oregon.
strings.facts.f2.label: Key books
strings.facts.f2.value: Extreme Programming Explained, Test-Driven Development: By Example and Tidy First?.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Short development feedback cycles
strings.highlights.h1.text: Promoted testing, collaboration and small changes through books on Extreme Programming and test-driven development.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Co-creating JUnit
strings.highlights.h2.text: Developed the Java unit-testing tool with Erich Gamma; its community continued its development.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discusses trust in AI development
strings.timeline.t1.text: Publishes an essay arguing that as AI accelerates code production, trust built through testing, review and collaboration remains an important constraint; this is the author’s view.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Tidy First? first released
strings.timeline.t2.text: The publisher records this as the first release of the first edition; the 2024 copyright year is not its initial publication year.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Publishes test-driven development textbook
strings.timeline.t3.text: Addison-Wesley publishes Test-Driven Development: By Example, introducing the practice through examples.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Helps create the Agile Manifesto
strings.timeline.t4.text: Joins 17 practitioners in Snowbird, Utah, on February 11–13 to formulate shared software-development values.
strings.timeline.t5.title: First Extreme Programming book published
strings.timeline.t5.text: The publisher dates the first edition of Extreme Programming Explained to this day; it systematically presents the method.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Collaborates on early JUnit
strings.timeline.t6.text: Early user Martin Fowler recalls Beck and Erich Gamma pair-programming the first version on a flight to OOPSLA; this is not a precise public release date.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Co-presents CRC-card teaching
strings.timeline.t7.text: His OOPSLA paper with Ward Cunningham describes teaching object-oriented thinking with class, responsibility and collaborator cards.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Co-authors pattern-language report
strings.timeline.t8.text: Writes a technical report with Ward Cunningham applying Christopher Alexander’s pattern-language ideas to object-oriented interface design; this is the report date.
